summary: This is a cheap, rule-clean tuning of master's own split-KV kernels and no landed hypothesis confounds it. The expected gain is about 1-3% on full decode_32, which works out to about 0.4% of the headline, so it can only be judged from the splitkv_attn_kernel and splitkv_combine_kernel rows; the hypothesis assumes tail quantization does not change, which is its weakest point and could cancel the gain.
justification: Mechanism, partly plausible. SMEM_A is about 91 KB at 1024 (ring 64 KB + idx 8 KB + q 2 KB + acc 16 KB + small arrays) and about 99 KB at 2048, so 2 CTAs per SM (198 KB) still fit; registers and __launch_bounds__(256,2) are unchanged. Combine: FINDINGS shows splitkv_combine_kernel at 8.2 us for decode_16 (about 1250 partials) and 8.4 us for decode_32 (about 2500), so its time does NOT scale with partial bytes (10 MB). It scales with the per-request serial loop. n = ceil(len/1024) is about 80 at both batches, the 4 warps walk it c += 4 (about 20 dependent iterations), and both grids fit in one wave. Halving n per request does shorten that chain, but the saving will be closer to 2-3 us than 4 us because launch latency and the reduce/epilogue stay fixed. The bytes argument in `expected` is the wrong reason, though the direction is right. Kernel A: each item end costs one __syncthreads, a 4-warp smem merge and a 4 KB partial store. There are about 9.6 item ends per CTA out of about 246 us, so halving them saves well under 1 us per CTA (about 0.3-0.5%), less than the 1-2% claimed. WEAKEST LINK, tail quantization: `about 5 vs 10 items per CTA, unchanged on average` is wrong in expectation. Agentic lengths are uniform in 80000 +/- 7.5% and redrawn on every call, so the total item count (about 2530 at 1024, about 1265 at 2048, over grid 264) moves by about +/-19 items per call and the fractional part of items/CTA is effectively random. The expected makespan excess of round-robin assignment is about 0.5 item: about 512 tokens at 1024 versus about 1024 at 2048, on about 9.8K tokens per CTA. That is roughly +5% of kernel A in the worst, latency-bound model, partly softened because early-finishing CTAs free HBM bandwidth (kernel A runs at about 51% of SoL). Padding also grows: every item runs all TILES tiles, so each request's last partial item averages 1024 instead of 512 masked tokens (32 requests x 512 extra tokens, about 0.65% extra MMA/softmax work with no loads). Net: combine about -2 to -3 us, kernel A anywhere from about -1 us to +several us, depending on the per-call quantization draw. Shape and weight consistency: full decode_32 is weighted 16, giving 3870 of the 4983 us decode_32 load. A 2-3 us gain on 242 us is about 1%, about 0.8% of the load and about 0.13-0.4% of the headline after the 6-load geomean, which is far inside the +/-1.5% CI and the 6% drift FINDINGS reports for this shape between identical runs. The `flat` expectations for decode_16, every sliding shape, verify and decode_1 are correct: the gate is batch >= 32 inside _splitkv_gate, which already excludes them. decode_16 is rightly left at 1024, since 2048 there would give about 2.4 items per CTA and a much worse tail.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: this is the code being tuned (CHUNK, the item schedule, the combine), so it is the base rather than a confounder. No revert makes sense: without it the change has nothing to act on.

sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: it touches only sliding shapes, yet its run reported a gain on full decode_32. Shape-level drift of a few percent on full decode_32 is therefore the noise floor for this hypothesis, so the headline and the shape median cannot be trusted at the expected 1% effect; read the splitkv kernel rows in top_kernels.

fused-preattention-triton, fa3-hdim128-head-pairing, paired-heads-launch-cleanup (+ab-tune-batch-gate), sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: none touches the split-KV launch pair or its memory traffic (the pairing is explicitly disabled when splitkv is gated on; the pre-attention kernel only produces q, about 2 us and unchanged). No interaction.
interference: No companion is warranted. top_kernels already reports kernel A and the combine separately, which is the attribution the hypothesis needs. A combine gain with a kernel-A loss would read directly as 'fewer partials help the combine, but the coarser tail costs more in kernel A', and that is the actionable answer either way. No landed hypothesis shares the launch sequence, so ab-revert has no target. The ab-tune / control candidates (chunk 1536, or 2048 with a smaller grid) would map out the item-size curve, but they cost a check for an effect of about 0.3% headline and would not make a single result more interpretable than the per-kernel rows already do. Better still: compute the 1024 vs 2048 per-CTA item quantization analytically at import (or offline) for lengths drawn from U[74000, 86000] x 32 at grid 264, and record it in the attempt file, so a kernel-A regression can be checked against the predicted tail. Sequencing: if full-cuda-onelaunch-warpspec-bulk-gather (running) lands and passes its self-check, it replaces both kernels at 1 < B <= 64 and this idea is moot. Also, splitkv-combine-wide-mlp (queued) targets the same combine latency, so whichever of the two lands second will see a smaller combine gain.
open_questions: Does kernel A get slower at 2048 because of the tail? Compare splitkv_attn_kernel's row (245.9 us baseline) on its own; if it grows by more than the combine shrinks, try a schedule fix (for example, assigning each request's last partial item first, or an LPT-like order over the prefix sum) instead of a bigger chunk.

Is the combine's 8.4 us mostly launch and fixed latency? Its near-identical time at decode_16 (8.2 us, half the partials) suggests that only the per-request loop length matters. A combine that splits the c loop over more warps, or the PDL/fusion items already queued, may be the better lever than halving the items.

Self-check coverage: confirm the 32-request synthetic case (the lens list repeated) actually takes the 2048 branch, runs at both the device grid and grid 3 at 2048, and includes a length exactly at a 2048 boundary (for example 2048 and 4096) as well as 4097 and 1025, so that a mismatch between the CHUNK of the attn kernel and the combine template would be caught.
